title: Ancient human skeleton discovered in Mexico dates back 13,000 years, analysis reveals
summary: A human skeleton discovered during archaeological excavations at the Felipe Ángeles International Airport (AIFA) in the State of Mexico has been dated to approximately 13,000 years ago, placing it among the oldest human remains ever identified in the Basin of Mexico. Named Yotzin, the exceptionally well-preserved individual provides new evidence of the populations that inhabited the region at the end of the Pleistocene and the beginning of the Holocene, offering researchers a rare opportunity to investigate the origins and lifestyles of some of the earliest inhabitants of the Americas. The findings were announced by Mexico's National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH), following laboratory analyses conducted in Belgium and the United States. The results establish Yotzin as one of the 23 oldest human skeletons known from the Basin of Mexico, a region whose prehistoric past continues to emerge through archaeological investigations. title: Phyllida Barlow's radical approach to sculpture explored in first Austrian museum exhibition
summary: Kunsthalle Krems is presenting Phyllida Barlow: Challenging Sculpture, the first museum solo exhibition in Austria devoted to the British artist Phyllida Barlow (1944–2023). Bringing together installations, sculptures, maquettes, paintings, and works on paper, the exhibition offers a comprehensive look at the extraordinary body of work of one of the most influential sculptors of her generation. The exhibition opened on November 21, 2026, and continues through March 29, 2027. "The exhibition at Kunsthalle Krems makes the full breadth of Phyllida Barlow's work accessible in Austria for the first time," said Florian Steininger, Artistic Director of Kunsthalle Krems. "In doing so, we make a significant contribution to the international discourse surrounding one of the most important sculptors of our time. title: Step inside the story with Toni Dove's immersive Installation at the McNay
summary: Visitors to the McNay Art Museum can become immersed in a sci-fi love story, interacting with virtual characters across time, in Toni Dove’s “Sunjammer 6: A Tale Blown by a Solar Breeze,” on view Nov. 21, 2026-Feb. 21, 2027. The mixed reality installation combines sculpture, installation, cinema and performance in a narrative that weaves ancient history, mathematics and astronomy with imagined futures. Dove describes “Sunjammer 6” as “a visual novel, a movie and a machine that tells stories.” The pioneering multimedia artist uses a custom-built interactive system that combines machine learning, skeletal tracking and multi-channel audio to respond to participants in real time. When visitors enter the exhibition, they activate the process and are drawn into another dimension. Cameras track movement, allowing a virtual character to react to their presence. title: Rare fossil discovery reveals new dinosaur species that were specialized fruit-eaters
summary: Among the ravenous carnivores and lumbering herbivores that roamed the Cretaceous landscape, another kind of dinosaur was evolving that started to eat something else: the plants that began to flower and produce fruit. The discovery by paleontologists from Stony Brook University, Royal Ontario Museum (ROM), and the North Dakota Geological Survey reveals a new species, Infernogallus jamesi – a type of small oviraptorosaur – had chewing muscles for mashing soft food, making it the first known dinosaur that specifically ate fruit. Led by Dr. Greg Funston, Assistant Professor in the Department of Anatomical Sciences at Stony Brook University, the research – which analyzed the chewing muscles of the new species, showing that it had a unique arrangement only seen in fruit-eating parrots today – was published in the journal Nature Communications. “We knew dinosaurs evolved to fill so many different roles

title: MoMA explores Philip Guston's haunting late paintings in "In the Studio"
summary: The Museum of Modern Art is presenting Philip Guston: In the Studio, an exhibition examining the intensely personal and politically charged paintings created during the final decades of the American artist's career. On view from November 21, 2026, through February 7, 2027, the exhibition brings together works that reveal Guston's distinctive visual language, in which ordinary objects, unsettling figures, and fragments of the human body become vehicles for exploring memory, history, violence, and the act of painting itself. "I've always had the feeling that art is nourished by the common and ordinary," Guston declared in 1980, the year of his death. His paintings frequently incorporated familiar objects such as cigarettes, light bulbs, shoes, and bottles, but transformed them into mysterious and often disturbing images. Disembodied

title: Folkert de Jong unveils neon acrylic plaster sculptures and food reliefs in 'The Party'
summary: Galerie Ron Mandos is presenting The Party, Folkert de Jong’s first solo exhibition at the gallery. Known for his theatrical sculptures that expose the darker side of power, history, and human nature, De Jong presents a new body of work that departs from his earlier practice, using acrylic plaster, neon and pastel pigments and a range of materials new to him. In The Party, a celebration appears carefully staged, yet behind the festive setting another reality gradually comes into view. De Jong has long been fascinated by the way big world problems originate in the smallest, most domestic settings; The Party provides the stage for this idea. What at first glance looks like a colorful celebration, reveals on closer inspection, the underlying relationships and discomfort. title: Claes Iversen designs new clothing collection for Rijksmuseum staff
summary: Dutch fashion designer Claes Iversen has designed a new clothing collection for Rijksmuseum staff. In January 2027, approximately 300 service and security staff at the museum will start wearing the new designs. Iversen has created a 12-piece collection that includes a blazer, trousers, a sweater, a dress, a bomber jacket and five accessories, including a scarf and a bow tie. The individual pieces can be combined in multiple ways, allowing staff to put together their own outfits. The base colour of the garments is a shade of brown inspired by 17th-century paintings in the museum, with white and black accents. "What struck me immediately was how much the Rijksmuseum values its employees – they are the public face of the organisation. From our very first conversations, their experiences were central to the process. I wanted to design clothes that they would feel comfortable in, and that would allow them to be themselves while also making them visibly part of one organisation." -- Cla

title: Legion of Honor presents Azzedine Alaïa's first major U.S. retrospective
summary: Azzedine Alaïa: Sculpting Fashion, the first major United States retrospective dedicated to the work of the famed couturier, opened November 21, 2026, at the Legion of Honor. Alaïa revolutionized fashion in the 1980s and 1990s by designing garments that celebrated the natural curves of women’s bodies, while also challenging the conventions and unrelenting pace of the fashion industry. The legacy of the Tunisian-born, Paris-based designer is defined by his compelling vision, technical sophistication, and uncompromising devotion to couture craftsmanship. The exhibition presents 80 garments from across Alaïa’s celebrated career as a designer, as well as pieces from his remarkable historical collections, from which he drew inspiration and technical understanding. title: Mark Handforth transforms urban fixtures, street signs, and light tubes in Berlin show
summary: For his first solo exhibition at Galerie Thomas Schulte, Mark Handforth presents Zig-Zag City - featuring new sculptural works that hang, twist, sprawl, and illuminate, together forming a dynamic landscape that responds to the site of the gallery. Here, Handforth continues to use motifs drawn from the fabric of the urban environment: its fixtures so ubiquitous as to be both immediately legible and almost unnoticeable. Recontextualized, rescaled, or reconfigured, these familiar elements take on new life and shifting narratives in relation to one another and to us. From the expansive streets intersecting the gallery's Corner Space, a clear form quickly comes into view: that of a large floating star. Titled Südstern / Blue Southern Star, like the plaza in Berlin-Kreuzberg, it seems to mark a location, as though an icon on a map. The star acts as a signpost through its material. title: National Gallery of Ireland marks 400 years since Jan Steen's birth with free exhibition
summary: 400 years after the birth of Jan Steen (1626–1679) – one of the leading Dutch painters of his time – the National Gallery of Ireland hosts an intimate, FREE exhibition that looks at the variety of his extensive career. Jan Steen: Sacred and Profane features seven works by the artist from Leiden, drawn from the National Gallery of Ireland’s collection as well as important loans from the Rijksmuseum, Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen, the Bredius Collection, the Bute Collection, and the National Gallery, London. Celebrated for his satirical and chaotic domestic scenes, Steen’s name is still synonymous in the Dutch language with a disorderly household. But during his prolific career he also produced history paintings, portraits and refined genre scenes. This exhibition highlights the variety of subject matters, united by his lively and characterful approach to painting. title: Exhibition exploring the power and splendor of ancient Maya civilization attracts over 47,000 visitors in Denmark
summary: An exhibition exploring the political power, artistic achievements, and cultural legacy of the ancient Maya civilization has attracted more than 47,000 visitors to the Moesgaard Museum in Aarhus, Denmark. Titled The Lordship Beneath the Jungle: Dzibanché and Calakmul, the exhibition brings together 167 archaeological objects and artworks, including extraordinary jade and shell funerary masks that are being displayed outside Mexico for the first time. Organized by Mexico's Ministry of Culture, through the National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH), in collaboration with the Moesgaard Museum, the exhibition opened in early October 2026 and had welcomed 47,335 visitors by November 17. title: Bowers Museum unveils new permanent gallery celebrating 3,000 years of Mexican and Central American art
summary: Bowers Museum, Orange County’s largest and most established global arts destination, announced today the unveiling of a new permanent gallery, Art of Mexico and Central America. The new installation brings together extraordinary works spanning more than 3,000 years of artistic and cultural history. Guest curated by Getty Research Institute scholar Dr.Khristaan Villela, the installation explores the rich traditions of Mesoamerican civilizations and their enduring influence on contemporary art and culture. Featuring ceremonial objects, intricate jewelry, ancient ceramics, and monumental artwork, the gallery invites visitors to discover the creativity, innovation, and cultural traditions that continue to connect generations. “At Bowers Museum, we believe art can educate people about cultures, history, and communities. title: Marc Selwyn Fine Art presents acrylic-on-jute paintings by Madrid artist Antonio Ballester Moreno
summary: Marc Selwyn Fine Art is presenting an exhibition of paintings made between 2019 and 2021 by Madrid-based artist Antonio Ballester Moreno. Working in acrylic on jute, Ballester Moreno draws on the recurring forms and rhythms of the natural world. Circles suggest suns or planets, bands of color establish horizons, and leaves repeat along a stem. Across the exhibition, these forms bring the scale of a growing plant into relation with the sweep of a landscape and the movement of celestial bodies. Repetition gives the paintings a sense of time. A yellow disc shifts against a steady horizon, registering a change in the sky. Elsewhere, circles cluster or spread across fields of red, drawing the eye along horizontal bands or sending it from one form to the next. The coarse weave of the jute remains visible throughout. title: Light and Space pioneer Lita Albuquerque unites painting, sculpture, and film in Palm Springs solo show
summary: Palm Springs Art Museum is presenting Lita Albuquerque: Cosmic Land, a solo exhibition on view October 16, 2026 through May 3, 2027. Spanning nearly six decades of her practice, the exhibition marks the first time the celebrated California artist's paintings, sculptures, installations, and films are brought together in a single exhibition. Guiding viewers through a continuous, unfolding journey, Cosmic Land traces the relationship between Earth and cosmos, revealing the terrestrial and celestial as inseparable and the human being as belonging to both at once. Albuquerque's work conveys that the ground beneath our feet is deeply entwined with the broader universe, carrying within it memory, consciousness, and starlight, or as the artist herself wrote in 2014, that "light carries information." title: Areum Yang explores distance, memory, and domestic space in new New York solo show
summary: Derek Eller Gallery is presenting a solo exhibition of new works by Areum Yang. Combining both wet and dry materials (charcoal, pencil, collage, pastel, acrylic, oil), Yang creates gestural, vivid paintings of dream-like environments which speak to notions of dislocation and home. She explains, Living in New York, I often speak with my family in Korea late at night, when it's already morning or afternoon there. Sometimes I feel as though I'm living in two different days at once, experiencing another part of the world while remaining physically in one place. This year, my parents moved back into the house where I spent much of my early childhood. The house is still there, but the people who once filled it have grown older, moved away, or passed away. title: Abel Alejandre expands his ongoing 'Xicanoland' counter-archive with borderless landscapes at LAUNCH Gallery
summary: LAUNCH Gallery and The National Tourism Board of Xicanoland present new paintings by celebrated Mexican-American artist Abel Alejandre. Scenic: Landscapes of an Empire is the third installment of Xicanoland, an ongoing body of work, built in chapters, that continues to expand as a living counter-archive. In this new series we present the nation itself: a contiguous tapestry of confederated states comprising plains our surveyors mapped, coastlines our fleets charted, valleys where the first launchpads rose, and skylines beneath our sky gods. title: Portrait photographer Mariana Cook turns her gaze to rocks that have been travelling for millennia
summary: For eleven years, American photographer Mariana Cook, a former apprentice of Ansel Adams, travelled across the world searching for glacial erratics: ancient boulders carried vast distances by glaciers and deposited far from their geological origins. The result is Out of Place – Out of Time, a compelling meditation on displacement, time and belonging, presented this November at Kulturstiftung Basel H. Geiger | KBH.G. The exhibition is curated by Swiss creative director and curator Beda Achermann and marks the first major presentation of this eleven-year body of work. From Martha’s Vineyard to some of the world’s most remote landscapes, Cook approaches these wandering rocks with the same intensity of observation that defined her celebrated portraiture, transforming seemingly inanimate geological forms into individual presences. summary: François Ghebaly is presenting CH3–CH2–O–CH2–CH3, a group exhibition on view at the gallery’s downtown Los Angeles location. title: MoMA PS1 presents 'Hard Art,' a major survey of abstraction by Black artists from 1969 to today
summary: MoMA PS1 presents Hard Art, a major exhibition that examines the legacy of abstraction by Black artists in the US from 1969 to today. On view through March 15, 2027, the exhibition features over 90 works by more than 40 artists, and juxtaposes historical paintings by artists who came to prominence in the 1970s with recent conceptually driven practices that incorporate sculpture, video, sound, and painting. The exhibition traces the legacy of three generations of artists, featuring the work of Frank Bowling, Mark Bradford, Peter Bradley, Barbara Chase-Riboud, Ed Clark, Melvin Edwards, Jennie C. summary: The Thomas Cole National Historic Site announcedrecently that two major paintings by Thomas Cole (1801-1848) have been gifted to the permanent collection of the historic site. title: Krist Gruijthuijsen appointed Director of the Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam
summary: The Supervisory Board of the Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam has appointed Krist Gruijthuijsen as the museum's new Director. He will succeed Rein Wolfs in July 2027. Krist Gruijthuijsen (born in Geldrop, the Netherlands, in 1980) has built an impressive career both in the Netherlands and internationally over the past two decades. Since 2025, he has been Director of EMMA – Espoo Museum of Modern Art in Finland, where his program places Northern European modern and contemporary art and design in a broader global context. From 2016 to 2024, he directed KW Institute for Contemporary Art in Berlin, helping shape it into the autonomous institution it is today. title: Group show at Galerie Guido W. Baudach explores contemporary approaches to the art of collage
summary: Galerie Guido W. title: Exhibition unveils rare maki-e lacquerware gifted by the Avant family and estate
summary: “Adorned in Gold: Japanese Lacquer from the Jacqueline Avant Collection” debuts the collection of the late Jacqueline Avant (1940–2021) and her singular passion for Japanese maki-e, dark lacquer objects sprinkled with gold powder and intended for both everyday use and grand affairs. Open Saturday, Nov. 21, through Sunday, Jan. 2, 2028, at the Smithsonian’s National Museum of Asian Art, the exhibition represents the first public reveal of these objects after they were gifted to the museum by the Avant family and estate. Jacqueline Avant, a leading figure for community engagement in Los Angeles and icon of the African American community, curated one of the most extensive and celebrated private collections of Japanese maki-e in the United States. “Adorned in Gold” is part of the museum’s celebration of American women art collectors

title: Laurent Grasso's work on view in historic artist homes of Frederic Church and Thomas Cole
summary: The Olana Partnership, the New York State Office of Parks, Recreation, and Historic Preservation, and the Thomas Cole National Historic Site announced a joint exhibition of work by acclaimed French conceptual artist Laurent Grasso in the historic artist homes of Frederic Church and Thomas Cole. Metaphysical Maze: Laurent Grasso at Frederic Church's Olana and the Thomas Cole Site opened on November 22, 2026, and run through March 28, 2027. This exhibition is a capstone celebration of Frederic Church 200, a year celebrating the bicentennial of Church’s birth. The exhibition accompanies a primary exhibition of Laurent Grasso’s work at MASS MoCA in North Adams, MA: Metaphysical Maze, the largest solo exhibition to date in the United States devoted to the artist. Metaphysical Maze at MASS MoCA is curated by Denise Markonish.

title: Sandra Wilson appointed President & CEO of ROM Governors as Janice Price announces retirement
summary: ROM Governors, the Foundation responsible for generating philanthropic support for the Royal Ontario Museum (ROM) and its mission, announced a leadership transition as President & CEO Janice Price plans to retire following a distinguished career in arts, culture, and philanthropy leadership. Seasoned fundraising executive Sandra Wilson, the Foundation's Chief Operating & Financial Officer, has been appointed its next President & CEO. Price will conclude her tenure on December 31, 2026. Over more than two years, Price strengthened ROM Governors as a vital partner to the Museum while advancing philanthropic support for key institutional priorities.
